newsitem.title: GERMANY: Many sports dipping in German TV ratings.
newsitem.headline: Many sports dipping in German TV ratings.

text.p: Sports like tennis, ice hockey and handball are dipping in popularity on German television and need to improve their image, market research institute Sport & Markt said on Thursday.

Only soccer has maintained its popularity with teenagers and adults among German television spectator sports in recent years, holding onto the number one sport, said Hartmut Zastrow, director of Sport & Markt.
"Sports that want to survive need a new concept," he said, adding that boxing and auto racing were growing more popular.

Sports from the United States are eclipsing more traditional German athletic events in general popularity among teens, Zastrow said. As part of their study, Sport & Markt polled 1,006 German teenagers interested in sports.
Among Germans between the ages of 12 and 19, basketball was the favourite sport, well ahead of soccer, and U.S. basketball player Michael Jordan topped the list of best athletes.
Zastrow said not a single soccer player appeared among the top ten sports idols of young people.
Another study jointly released by television marketing company IP Deutschland found that sports are more important for teenagers than for adults.
About 44 percent of 14 to 19 year old Germans take part in athletics several times a week, while just under 13 percent play sports among those over 20, IP Deutschland said.
